title: order of get_property_list() for C# scripts differs between editor and exported projects
body:
### Tested versions

tested 4.7.rc.mono, 4.0.stable.mono 4.1.stable.mono

### System information

Godot v4.7.rc.mono (691664bf4) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:58:02 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (nvidia; 610.43.02) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.25 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Pseudocode referred to in description
``` C#
[ExportGroup(Group1)]
[Export] var property1;
[Export] var property2;
```

When calling get_property_list on a class with a C# script running in the editor. The order is as you world expect
- builtin properties...
- Group1
- property1
- property2 

but in an exported build the property list will reverse the script properties
 - builtin properties...
 - property2
 - property1
 - Group1
 
in modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp there's a couple of snippets like the one below. where in exported builds push_front is called when iterating through member_info.
``` C++
#ifdef TOOLS_ENABLED
	for (const PropertyInfo &prop : script->exported_members_cache) {
		props.push_back(prop);
	}
#else
	for (const KeyValue<StringName, PropertyInfo> &E : script->member_info) {
		props.push_front(E.value);
	}
#endif
```

### Steps to reproduce

Run the project in the editor look at console output or onscreen text. Then export the project and run the exported project.
With the MRP you'll see that the section of the property list that contains the c# properties is ordered [group1,number1,number2] in the editor and reversed in the exported build

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[TestProject.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31283960/TestProject.tar.gz)
